summary: I tested the pixel fail's attribution, TRICERATOPS's blocker, NFPP and apertures, the star's companions and radial velocities, the secondary and second signal, the transit depths, SPOC's own S12 DV report and the literature. The pixel fail measured a catalogued variable star (Gaia DR3 VARIABLE, 2' away), the target's PRF carries the transit in every sector, and nothing shows an eclipsing binary, a companion or a prior claim. The row still can't pass TRICERATOPS: its NFPP of 0.0067, almost all from the dwarf TIC 423100450 34" out, sits between the bars whatever the blocker does, and ground-based photometry of a transit would decide it.

findings.claim: TRICERATOPS can't pass this row on the public data even with its blocker cleared: the mean NFPP of 0.0067 sits between the 0.001 pass bar and the 0.1 fail bar, and 95% of it is one dwarf 34" out, TIC 423100450, which the pixels argue against but TRICERATOPS can't take in; seeing-limited ground-based photometry of a predicted transit would decide it.

TIC 423100450 is Gaia DR3 5836453499849306752: 34.1" in neighbours.csv, Tmag 11.96, required depth 0.96% (neighbours.csv) and 1.31% (TRICERATOPS tdepth); Gaia DR3 parallax 2.71 mas (S/N 199), Teff 5955 K, logg 4.18, radius 1.22 Rsun (gaiadr3.gaia_source joined with astrophysical_parameters on the Gaia TAP): a dwarf that can host a 4.3 h transit at 14.19 d. The other bright stars near the target are giants and get about 1e-52 in probs.csv: TIC 423105440 (15.0", Gaia DR3 5836453499849301760, parallax 0.267 mas, logg 2.0, radius_flame 18.4 Rsun) and TIC 423100457 (37.7", Gaia DR3 5836452842610251392, parallax 0.399 mas, G 11.99, BP-RP 1.96). Inside 15" the only other possible host, Gaia DR3 5836452846954130944 (8.4", needs 84%), gets zero depth in TRICERATOPS. Pixels, outside the pipeline (a fixed-position PRF fit like the diagnosis's two_star.py, with the target, TIC 423100450, 423100457, 423100455 and 423100496 held at their catalogue positions plus a constant, errors from the same fit to each sector's null images): MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl.exe -d Ubuntu-26.04 --cd /tmp/t13/423100454-1 -- /tmp/t13/heavy.sh ~/code/tess-hunt/.venv/bin/python multi_star.py multi_no5440.json 423100454 423100450 423100457 423100455 423100496, then .venv/bin/python exclude.py multi_no5440.json (outputs /tmp/t13/423100454-1/multi_no5440.txt and .json; the saved difference images of SECOND2_RUN, the sha256s in pixels.json). TIC 423100450's amplitude is 1.7 +- 3.3, 1.8 +- 11.9, 2.6 +- 5.2, -3.5 +- 13.7, -2.2 +- 11.1 e-/s in S103, S102, S65, S39, S12, against the 19.6, 24.3, 12.6, 19.7, 19.2 e-/s it would need as the host (the loss the target's aperture sees, 448 ppm x FLFRCSAP 0.83 x the fitted target flux; its aperture share is at most 1): pooled 0.08 +- 0.14 of that minimum (6.5 null sds below), 0.04 +- 0.30 (3.2 sds) from S12, S39 and S65 alone; TIC 423100455 5.4 and 1.9 sds. The target's amplitudes, 38.3 +- 11.1, 33.3 +- 11.0, 19.4 +- 16.5, 34.9 +- 62.1, 39.3 +- 35.9 e-/s, match the 30.1, 37.2, 19.3, 30.2, 29.4 that the PDCSAP depth (570 ppm) predicts on it. What would decide it: ground-based seeing-limited photometry at a predicted transit (checks.json windows, e.g. S113 BTJD 4426.145 and 4440.331, sd 10.2 min, or any epoch of the density-prior ephemeris) showing no 0.96 to 1.31% eclipse on TIC 423100450 and no 3.9 to 6.3% eclipse on TIC 423100455 (38.4"), or the dip on the target.

6. Inputs to exclude.py, from checks.json:
   - FLFRCSAP: S12 0.865, S39 0.828, S65 0.867.

F1 reads the rules correctly, and the hold fits the brief's definition.

1. Outcome rule. vet-v3.toml [triceratops] sets fpp_pass 0.5, nfpp_pass 0.001 and nfpp_fail 0.1. src/tess_hunt/tricera.py outcome() (about lines 85 to 121) passes only when mean FPP < 0.5 and mean NFPP < 0.001, and fails only when mean NFPP > 0.1. Anything else is inconclusive, with blockers checked first. Decision 0026's Outcomes section and M3 design 4.5 say the same.

2. The record. triceratops.json in drafts/m3-r2/423100454-1 is byte-identical (cmp) to TRIC3A_RUN 20261021T044850Z-vetting-triceratops-cd4e7a2-07c3, which runs on 0036's code. It gives nfpp_mean 0.006695 (sd 0.00085) and fpp_mean 0.0353, with blockers holding only "the neighbour table is inconclusive: 1 Gaia DR3 star(s) within the radius have no G magnitude". With that blocker removed, the code still returns inconclusive, as the claim says.

3. Bar 3. Decision 0028 bar 3 (M3 design 4.9) needs a TRICERATOPS pass, so the claim that it can't pass on the public data is a correct reading. Two other routes don't change that:
   - Contrast curves act on unresolved companions, not on resolved nearby stars, and none exist here.
   - QLP sectors are left out of TRICERATOPS (design 4.5, pin P3), so a QLP redelivery doesn't change its input.
   The 0032 caveat that NFPP can move with the ephemeris doesn't undercut this. 0026 fixes the input to the density-prior ephemeris, and NFPP would have to fall 6.7 times, far beyond 0036's run-to-run noise of 3e-3 relative.

4. Composition. Summing probs.csv by ID over NTP, NEB and NEBx2P gives an NFPP of 0.006485, matching that run's NFPP. TIC 423100450 has 0.006135 (94.6%) and TIC 423100455 has 0.000341 (5.3%). In triceratops.json hosts:
   - TIC 423100450: sep 34.13", required depth 0.963%, tdepth 1.312%.
   - TIC 423100455: sep 38.43", required depth 3.94%, tdepth 6.26%.
   - Inside 15", only 5836452846954130944 (8.42", tdepth 0) and the giant TIC 423105440 (14.98").
   The "95%" comes from the tenth run's probs.csv, the only scenario table the record keeps (0026), and the evidence says so. It is not an overstatement that changes the outcome: every run's NFPP (0.0055 to 0.0084) sits between the bars.

5. Rating.
   - The brief and 0028 define hold as: the public data can't decide, and the finding names what would. Ground-based photometry is on both lists. The windows it cites (S113 BTJD 4426.145 and 4440.331, sd 10.2 min) are in checks.json windows.
   - 0026 and 0028 send a hold on blending to ground-based work, not to the DDT ask. F1 rests on blending and doesn't ask for 2-min data.
   - The finding uses the out-of-pipeline PRF fit only to say the pixels "argue against" TIC 423100450, never to clear it. That respects 0033 item 5 (pixels.py frozen, the diagnosis gates nothing).
   - It gives both pooled numbers: with the timing-suspect sectors (6.5 sds) and without them (3.2 sds). 0022's timing exclusion covers the QLP light curves, not TESScut images.
   - 0033 item 3 leaves stars within 15" to TRICERATOPS. TIC 423100450 at 34" is outside that, so naming it as the deciding neighbour is consistent.

findings.claim: TRICERATOPS's inputs hold up: the star without a G magnitude can't host the dip, so the blocker changes nothing; S65's aperture is the one the S65 photometry used; and the 62 dropped TIC rows don't matter.
findings.evidence: The no-G star is Gaia DR3 5836452881314264576 (~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/423100454-1/checks.json neighbours.evidence.no_g; neighbours.csv: 49.8" out, tmag_from none). Gaia DR3 (/tmp/t13/423100454-1/queries.sh): phot_g_n_obs 0, no BP, RP 19.504 from 6 RP observations, astrometric_params_solved 3 (no parallax or proper motion). Stassun et al. eq. 1 (src/tess_hunt/neighbours.py:40-43) with Gaia's G-RP colours puts T within about 0.1 mag of RP for BP-RP 0 to 3, so T is about 19.4 to 19.6. It would need T 17.00 or brighter to need even a total eclipse (8.6228 + 2.5 log10(1/0.000448)); at T 19.4 it needs 920% (448 ppm x 10^(0.4 x (19.4 - 8.6228))). Without the blocker TRICERATOPS stays inconclusive on NFPP (F1). S65: tricera.apertures (src/tess_hunt/tricera.py:333-368) takes SPOC 2-min sectors from TRICERATOPS's get_spoc_apertures and TESS-SPOC sectors from the light-curve file's APERTURE extension (bit 2). The run log's 'No SPOC aperture for sector(s) 65' (~/.cache/tess-hunt/logs/m3-rerun-tric3-five.log lines 16 and 40) is get_spoc_apertures' warning, which the code doesn't use for a TESS-SPOC sector. Read through heavy.sh (/tmp/t13/423100454-1/peek_lc.py): hlsp_tess-spoc_tess_phot_0000000423100454-s0065_tess_v1_lc.fits has CRVAL1P 416, CRVAL2P 613 and 14 bit-2 pixels, the same 14 (column, row) pairs as triceratops.json apertures.65.ccd_pixels, and its CROWDSAP 0.79285467 is the one checks.json records; target_in_aperture is true in both sectors. S12 took its 12-pixel SPOC aperture; S39 (600 s) was left out as slower than the 200 s group. Dropped: triceratops.json dropped_stars holds 61 DUPLICATE rows, each naming the kept TIC it duplicates, and one ARTIFACT, TIC 423100507, which the MAST TIC (Mast.Catalogs.Filtered.Tic) gives as Tmag 15.6, 62.8" from the target, no Gaia id: outside the 1' table and too faint to matter.

findings.evidence: Seeded fits (/tmp/pixel-diag/seed_check.txt): S102 7.3" at quality 0.12, S65 7.0" at 0.17. The same sectors' no-transit images reach higher qualities (/tmp/pixel-diag/nulls_423.py: S102 up to 0.29 at phase 0.575 and 0.27 at 0.850; S65 up to 0.44 at 0.850, 0.38, 0.36, 0.34), so those seeded fits are no more PRF-like than noise. The check's own fits that sit near the target: S103 (+3.8" E, +4.3" N) 5.7" at q 0.52, above all 14 nulls (best 0.34); S39 (+3.7, -4.5) 5.8" at q 0.73, nulls best 0.37; S12 (+3.2, -8.1) 8.7" at q 0.57, nulls best 0.49. Fixed fit (/tmp/t13/423100454-1/multi_no5440.txt): target z 3.5 (S103), 3.0 (S102), 1.2 (S65), 0.6 (S39), 1.1 (S12); pooled 599 +- 124 ppm (z 4.8) with all five, 638 +- 378 ppm (z 1.7) without S102 and S103. The diagnosis's box z at the star (section 2): 4.7, 5.4, 3.2, 1.9, 1.5 against 3.7, 6.6, 3.5, 1.6, 1.4 expected (S103, S102, S65, S39, S12). S102 and S103 are flagged because QLP's barycentric timestamps are wrong there (decisions 0010, 0022); the pixel check builds its images from TESScut FFI cutouts (t13/pixel-epoch.md, code path), not from QLP, so the flag does not reach them, and their box z matching the expected z shows the windows sit on transits. The outcome: ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/423100454-1/pixels.json gives S102 quality 0.91653 and S65 0.91611; without S102, S65's 115.7" is the best-quality sector and the check fails the same way. Kepler's law for a 1.0 Msun star at P 14.186 d, edge-on: K = 8.25 km/s for 0.1 Msun, 1.74 km/s for 0.02 Msun (python one-liner, G 6.674e-11). ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/423100454-1/checks.json: shape grazing probability 0.0, b 0.45 (flat fit) and 0.21 (density-prior fit); density tension 0.9 sigma; Rp 2.33 and 2.27 Earth radii. probs.csv: EB 1.4e-43, EBx2P 2.8e-28.

findings.claim: The transits are fully covered and spread evenly (two per sector, none near a gap), but the depths scatter: S39 is the deepest sector and S65's two transits differ by about 2.4 sigma; the QLP depths are about 0.8 of PDCSAP's, as 0010's QLP dilution allows.
findings.evidence: lc_events.py (F8's command): E0 642 +- 90, E1 489 +- 82 (S12); E52 781 +- 80, E53 738 +- 83 (S39); E102 366 +- 79, E103 754 +- 84 (S65); evidence only: E176 465 +- 69, E177 404 +- 74 (S102), E178 618 +- 86 (S103) ppm. E102 minus E103 is 388 ppm, 3.4 sigma white, about 2.4 with S65's red-noise beta 1.41 (~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/423100454-1/checks.json red_noise). Gaps printed by the same script: every vet-kept transit sits at least 2.1 d from a gap and 3.9 d from a sector edge. checks.json sector_depth: S12 479 +- 77, S39 706 +- 67, S65 474 +- 79 ppm, p 0.030 (bar 0.001); holdout tensions 1.26, 2.42, 1.56 (bar 3.0). CROWDSAP 0.840, 0.858, 0.793; TIC contratio 0.252. ~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/423100454-1/checks-with-suspect.json: QLP S102 369 +- 115, S103 565 +- 120 ppm (mean 462, p 0.24), 0.81 of the PDCSAP mean 570; decision 0010 found QLP depths at 0.60 to 0.99 of SPOC's on crowded stars. The scatter fits 0031's causes (crowding, red noise) and decides nothing.

findings.claim: No paper names the star a planet host, eclipsing binary, variable or multiple, no TOI or CTOI exists, and the signal is public only as SPOC's S12 TCE and ExoMiner's planet-candidate rows.
findings.evidence: literature.json in LIT3_RUN (signals/423100454-1) equals the draft's (sorted-key diff); its 24 hits all came from ADS's object search, and arXiv, OpenAlex and Zenodo found 0 for all six names; every source's result there carries from_run 20261020T091938Z (LIT_RUN), so these searches date from 2026-10-20. None names the star as a host, binary, variable or multiple. Those whose dismissal isn't obvious from the title: 2019A&A...623A..72K and Kervella 2022 (no proper-motion anomaly, no CPM companion; F6); 2021ApJS..254...42B (HGCA chisq 0.866); 2004A&A...418..989N and 2009A&A...501..941H (no binary flag, 2 RVs, P(chi2) 0.837; F7); 2006AstL...32..759G and 2012A&A...546A..61D (RV compilations); 2016ApJ...826..171G (a row of its metallicity sample, [Fe/H] 0.03, VizieR J/ApJ/826/171); 2012MNRAS.427..343M (EIR 1.004, no infrared excess, J/MNRAS/427/343); 2017AJ....154..115H (its photon-sail trajectories cover about 22,000 stars within about 300 ly, per arXiv 1704.03871's abstract; the star is at 69 pc). ExoFOP read live on 2026-10-21 returned a maintenance page ('System Calibration in Progress'), so the dossier's ExoFOP read (LIT3_RUN, status ok, no TOI, CTOI or planet) is the latest; NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP, toi table where tid=423100454: no rows (queries.sh). SIMBAD lists HD 142959 as PM*, G6IV/V, with no binary or variable type. Public detections: SPOC's S12 TCE 01 with DV products on MAST (F5) and ExoMiner rows 423100454-1-S12 (v1 and v2 2-min) and 423100454-1-S39 (v2 FFI, score 0.785, PC) (~/.cache/tess-hunt/drafts/m3-r2/423100454-1/checks.json novelty). Decision 0033's promotion names the ExoMiner row; the SPOC TCE is missing from the second list's table (F5).
